messages:
tanvi: Heads-up: onboarding morpheus13b int4. canary shows rare OOMs when several 1k+ gen requests align. pattern looks different from previous: OOMs on mid-decode when prefetch waves overlap but after async-compact already enabled. repro gist linked.

rafi: interesting. what's the runtime/kernel and exact flags?

tanvi: runtime 2.4.0, kernel=optimized-attn-v2. args:
```
--quant=int4 --prefetch=true --batch-size=10 --max_new_tokens=1600 --kv_reserve=0.18 --microbatch_pacing=off
```
log snip:
```
[2026-03-24T02:14:03Z] kv_prefetch miss burst 67%
[2026-03-24T02:14:03Z] slab stripe expand 96->256MB
[2026-03-24T02:14:03Z] GPU alloc fail 72MB -> OOM
```

sasha: can you repro with 3 concurrent 1200-token calls? also which node family?

tanvi: repro script: https://internal/ci/repro/morpheus-adaptive-repro.sh. GPUs: A10G and A100-mig mixed in canary pool. yes repros on A10G nodes primarily.

rafi: hypothesis: residual nondeterministic allocation patterns when multiple prefetched KV waves hit slab allocator simultaneously. earlier work helped but the root is the fixed kv_reserve + synchronized microbatch starts. two orthogonal levers: make kv_reserve adaptive per-request (based on estimated tokens + recent node pressure) and enable microbatch pacing to desync prefetch start times.

tanvi: I prototyped adaptive kv_reserve: reserve = clamp(0.12, 0.12 + 0.00006*estimated_tokens, 0.30) and a node_pressure_factor that bumps reserve by up to +0.05 when slab_growth_rate > threshold. paired with microbatch_pacing that spreads prefetch start across 100-500ms window. ran local stress: 0 OOMs across 2k runs.

sasha: nice. what's latency impact?

tanvi: p95 +10% on A10G, p95 +3% on A100. throughput per-GPU drops ~6% at extreme. tradeoff seems acceptable for canary.

rafi: risks: adaptive reserve could starve smaller requests if miscomputed. add guard: per-request min_reserve=0.12, max_reserve=0.30, and don't exceed node free threshold. Also add metrics: per-request kv_reserve_used, reserve_adjust_reason.

sasha: and add a quick fallback: if alloc fails after reserve bump, short-circuit to int8 variant or to kernel=v1 for that request. prefer int8 route for quality-sensitive ones.

ci-bot: scheduled jobs: morpheus-adaptive-kv-smoke (50 long-turn traces, concurrency 4), morpheus-microbatch-pacing-smoke. thresholds: 0 OOMs, p95 <= baseline*1.20.

devops-bot: rolled flag experiment: feature.flag morpheus.adaptive_kv enabled for canary cohort (4% traffic). logging hooks added: slab_growth_rate, reserve_offsets, stagger_offsets.

tanvi: patch in PR: https://internal/pr/4512. runtime.config snippet:
```
adaptive_kv:
  enabled: true
  formula: "0.12 + 6e-5*est_tokens"
  min: 0.12
  max: 0.30
microbatch_pacing:
  enabled: true
  window_ms: 100-500
fallback:
  on_alloc_fail: route_int8_if_quality_sensitive
```

rafi: before expanding, add a small CI A/B quality eval for the long-list patterns (20 prompts) to ensure no >3% token-acc drop.

ci-bot: added morpheus-adaptive-kv-quality-a_b. threshold: token-acc delta <= 3% vs int8 baseline.

sasha: monitoring guidance: add dashboard panels for reserve distribution, stagger offset histogram, and per-node slab tail. set alert if average reserve >0.26 on >50% of nodes (might indicate runaway).

tanvi: initial telemetry after rolling to 4%: OOMs -> 0 in canary, avg reserve ~0.195, stagger offsets uniform across window, p95 +9% on A10G. CI smoke passing now. quality A/B running.

rafi: if quality A/B shows regressions on enumerations, fallback to routing those by token_estimate >800 to int8. also schedule a quant-recal job as a parallel mitigation.

sasha: agreed. open runtime ticket to make adaptive_kv tunable via console with per-cohort overrides and safe caps. add a note to runbook.

tanvi: done: runbook entry and console toggle doc linked in PR. holding canary at 4% for 3 hours then expand to 20% if no alerts and quality within limits.

ci-bot: adaptive-kv smoke passed (0 OOMs, p95 within threshold). quality A/B still running.

sasha: thanks. leaving thread open until A/B completes, but great progress. :thumbsup:
